metric_policy.all_requirements_covered: every fully_answerable requirement of the query is covered
metric_policy.duplicate_unit_in_ranking: first occurrence keeps the gain and the recall credit. A later copy occupies its rank with gain 0.
metric_policy.headline_population: answerability=fully_answerable and split=test, with at least one retrieval unit whose own judged relevance is >= 1
metric_policy.hit: raw top-k contains a unit with its own judged relevance >= 1
metric_policy.mrr: 1 / raw rank of the first unit with its own relevance >= 1, cutoff 20
metric_policy.ndcg_headline: condensed: skip unjudged units, keep judged relevance 0, gain 2^relevance-1, each retrieval_unit_id gains at most once, cutoff 10 on the condensed list
metric_policy.ndcg_sensitivity_unjudged_as_zero: raw top-10, unjudged gain 0 at that rank. Same unit-once rule. Not the headline. Equals condensed NDCG when the raw top-10 is fully judged.
metric_policy.preferred: diagnostic. A seed retrieval unit that remains judged relevant. Otherwise one fallback unit. Non-preferred can still be relevant.
metric_policy.recall_denominator: unique retrieval units with judged relevance >= 1
metric_policy.recall_micro: sum of retrieved relevant units / sum of relevant units
metric_policy.relevance_0: the unit was read and judged irrelevant
metric_policy.requirement_recall: requirements whose own relevant unit appears in the window, divided by the requirement count. Not by source elements.
metric_policy.retrieval_unit: the object the judge read and the object the retriever returns
metric_policy.shared_source_element: units that share an element stay separate. A grade is not copied onto another unit.
metric_policy.source_element: citation provenance only. Not a relevance row.
metric_policy.unjudged: absent from qrels. Never stored as relevance 0.

bm25.parameter_history: k1=1.2 and b=0.75 were introduced as pinned defaults in commit 236c2a3 and were not edited later. The only later bm25.py change added rank_all. The repository has no k1/b sweep. This run does not retune them and does not read v2.1 TEST. They are conventional BM25 defaults, not a dev-tuned operating point for this benchmark.

query_preprocessing.shared_input: question text with no expansion and no shared analyzer
bm25_tokenizer_rules: Numbers keep comma groups, then commas are removed
Hangul runs and ASCII words of length >= 2
Hangul surface form plus overlapping syllable bigrams when the run is longer than 2
Percent signs are stripped from numeric tokens
No stopword list and no morphological dictionary
Query term frequency is saturated at 1
Documents with score 0 are omitted from top-k
query_preprocessing.difference: Both retrievers receive the same raw question. Dense encodes it with the existing BGE-M3 query encoder and no instruction. BM25 applies NFKC and ko-mixed-v1, including Hangul syllable bigrams, and saturates query term frequency at 1.

filing_policy: resolve_search_call / select_filings with as_of, period, and report_types unset. Same helper as the v2.1 Dense-D2a rescore. Correction originals in scope are suppressed. BM25 indexes only the retrieval units inside that receipt set.
hybrid_decision_rule: Primary label uses DEV Hit@10 and requirement@10 only. B when BM25 recovers nothing Dense missed: BM25-only query hits are 0, BM25-only requirement recoveries are 0, and no query has crossed requirement coverage. C when that is not true and both-miss queries are at least as many as the two asymmetric query cells combined and at least one third of DEV. A otherwise, which requires BM25 to add a query hit, a requirement, or a crossed multi-requirement case without shared misses dominating. B takes precedence over C so a nested BM25 does not become a hybrid proposal. Shared-miss dominance still selects the non-hybrid follow-up.
